mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses equity discount rates and signals aggressive monetary easing, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In 10 consecutive months with UNRATE > 5.0% for two months, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand weakness that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS occurs in 15 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) triggers anticipated Federal Reserve tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as bond yields rise.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing activity and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO increases for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly employment growth exceeding 200,000 jobs signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In 12 consecutive months with PAYEMS > 200000, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) combined with high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%) signals monetary policy accommodation during economic weakness, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS < 1.0% AND UNRATE > 6.0%) occurs in 10 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong economic growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 2.0%) supports sustained corporate earnings expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 2.0%, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods over a 5-year rolling window.
